# New-ZbxTemplateGroup

## SYNOPSIS

Creates a template group.

## SYNTAX

```
New-ZbxTemplateGroup [[-Name] <string>] [-Uuid <string>] [-AdditionalProperty <Hashtable>] [-Force] [-InputObject <PSObject>] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

A template group is a named set of templates; permissions select templates by their groups. The New-ZbxTemplateGroup cmdlet sends templategroup.create with one request field per parameter, then reads the new template group back with templategroup.get and writes it. The server requires -Name; -AdditionalProperty sets any other field by its API name and wins over a parameter. -WhatIf shows what would be created, and the command needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Create a template group

```powershell
New-ZbxTemplateGroup -Name 'Templates/Applications' | Select-Object GroupId, Name
```

Writes the created group (templategroup.create, read back with templategroup.get). A / in the name nests it.

### Example 2: Create a group and put a template in it

```powershell
$group = New-ZbxTemplateGroup -Name 'Templates/Applications'
Set-ZbxTemplate -InputObject 'Web App' -Group 'Templates/Web', $group | Out-Null
Get-ZbxTemplate -Group $group | Select-Object TemplateId, HostName
```

The written group object can be passed on: -Group takes names, ids or objects. Set-ZbxTemplate -Group replaces the template's groups.

### Example 3: Preview the change first

```powershell
New-ZbxTemplateGroup -Name 'Templates/Applications' -WhatIf
```

ConfirmImpact is Medium: -WhatIf describes the create without sending it; -Confirm asks first.
